title: Rewrite the template cache for same filename?
body:
Ok, this is a weird use-case. But I have a few scripts for setting wallpapers on my system. But what the scripts do is basically copy the selected files to a standard location (~/.config/wall.png) and then set the wallpaper using swww/swaybg/fehbg etc. 

This makes it easier to reference my current wallpaper from any place, like rofi, thumbnails, firefox, lockscreens, etc. but when I use hellwal -i ~/.config/wall.png to set the colors, and then change my wallpaper, and rerun the command, it doesn't generate new colors, since the same cache/wall.png.XXX already exists. And I have to detele the cache to generate the colors again.

Is there a way to fix or overcome this issue?

Thanks
author: SwayKh

comments.body:
OH wait, I think just using --no-cache flag is enough.

I saw the flag before but I though the cache was important to source the colorscheme later, but the template are generated anyway, and the terminal colors just need the sourced terminal.sh.

I'll close the issue. Thanks for the awesome program!
I'm glad you make it work and that you like it! Happy ricing

title: Bug: Required Directories Not Created on First Run
body:
When running hellwal for the first time, the program does not create the required directories:

    ~/.cache/helwall
    ~/.config/template
    ~/.config/theme

As a result, it failed to cache it properly. 
but when i manually created the directory it works perfectly, idk if it is my problem, i did installed it using 

`
yay -S hellwal
`

I believe hellwal should have automatically created the directories if needed. 
i read the README files and i hope i didn't miss anything about this, if i have ,im soo sry.   

To reproduce it you can delete the above directories. 

Suggested Labels: bug, Question

OS: Arch Linux x86_64 
Kernel: 6.13.2-arch1-1 
WM: i3 
Hellwal: 1.0.2-1
author: Abhinav-VS21

comments.body:
I think for ease of use it should be created, but it was done intentionally, because program itself doesn't really need these folders. 

If you create some template in hellwal template folder in:

```sh
~/.config/hellwal/templates/
```

cache folder will be created automatically after using hellwal with generated content from template.

So like I said I don't think it's needed, but I see a lot of people don't like this approach so probalby next version will be with folders and some templates be default.


Also thank you for opening the issue :)

comments.body:
I've addressed the issue through a pull request, improving both hellwal.c and the Makefile for smoother compilation. Feel free to close this at your convenience. 

However, I have a few questions about the project:
1. Is it expected behavior for only one terminal to change color when running hellwal? I've noticed that in ST, only the terminal where I execute the command changes, while other open terminals and newly launched ones don't adopt the new colorscheme.
2. Should I add a hellwal command to my .xinitrc file to ensure it runs on system startup?
3. What other applications can benefit from hellwal? Would DWM or various X11 programs be compatible with it?

Hi, thank you for creating an issue and PR!

1. Hellwal should color all **currently** open terminals. If you want to have colored every new opened terminal, you have to create template file with colors and source it in ``.bashrc``. I've done it like this:

(these two hellwal templates are in repo in ``./templates`` folder)
```sh
dh » pwd
/home/dh/.config/hellwal
dh » tree
.
├── templates
│   ├── terminal.sh
│   └── variables.sh
```

And in the end of your bashrc put this:

```sh
source ~/.cache/hellwal/variables.sh
sh ~/.cache/hellwal/terminal.sh
``` 

2. You don't have to, after running hellwal it's saved to ``~/.cache``, you just have to somehow source or load generated files.
3. A lot, probably anything that can be set through some config file. I use hellwal for Firefox, Terminals, Discord, Duckduckgo, Hyprland, HellWM, Waybar.... There is a lot.

PS: I already merged **PR**, thank you :) 

Anything else would you like to know about Hellwal or how to use it?
